examples.knowledge_point: Approximating the Solution to an Initial Value Problem Using The Modified Euler Method With One Step
examples.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
y' = x^2y^2+xy^2, \qquad y(1)=1
$$

Use the modified Euler method with one step to approximate $y(2).$
examples.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
y' = f(x,y), \qquad y_0 = y(x_0),
$$

the modified Euler method with step size $\Delta x$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y'_p = f(x_\text{new},y_p)$ is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point $(x_\text{new}, y_p) = (x + \Delta x, y + \Delta y_p).$

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=2,$ we will use a step size of

$$
\Delta x = 2 - 1 = 1.
$$

First, we add the initial condition data to a table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now, we compute the value of $y'$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+x{y}^{2} \\  & ={1}^{2}\cdot {1}^{2}+1\cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ |  |  |  |  |

Next, we compute $\Delta y_p$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =2\cdot 1 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ |  |  |  |

The coordinates of the initially predicted new point given by the predictor equation are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=1+1=2, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=1+2=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add the second value to the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $3$ |  |  |

So, the predicted slope at this point is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{p}^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{p}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}\cdot {3}^{2}+2\cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =54.\end{aligned}
$$

We can add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $3$ | $54$ |  |

Finally, we compute $\Delta y$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+54)\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 56 \\  & =28\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $3$ | $54$ | $28$ |

The value of $x$ in the next row is $x_\text{new} = 2.$ To get the value of $y$ in the next row, we add $\Delta y$ to $y{:}$

$$
y_\text{new} = y + \Delta y = 1 + 28 = 29
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $3$ | $54$ | $28$ |
| $2$ | $29$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2) \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{29}.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x-3y,\,y(0)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the modified Euler method. Complete the first row of the table below, given that the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2}.$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} | {{field-5}} |
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the modified Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

First, we compute the value of ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2x-3y \\  & =2\cdot 0-3\cdot 1 \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $-3$ |  |  |  |  |

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(-3)\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this value to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $-3$ | $-\frac{3}{2}$ |  |  |  |

The coordinates of the initially predicted new point given by the predictor equation are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=0+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=1+(-\frac{3}{2})=-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add the second value to the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $-3$ | $-\frac{3}{2}$ | $-\frac{1}{2}$ |  |  |

So, the predicted slope at this point is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & =f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p}) \\  & =2\cdot {x}_{\text{new}}-3\cdot {y}_{p} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}-3\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $-3$ | $-\frac{3}{2}$ | $-\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{5}{2}$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-3+\frac{5}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed first row is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $-3$ | $-\frac{3}{2}$ | $-\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{5}{2}$ | $-\frac{1}{8}$ |
